scope: Priority 1: Linux process-capture ownership and cleanup on the existing REA VPS
cause: Native Linux kernel-thread candidates (PPID=2, PGID=0, UID=0) expose no process environment; strict ownership sweep previously treated them as possibly capture-owned and returned cleanup_incomplete.
safety_guards: Kernel process relation requires stable native before/after observation and process table match
Retained or token-verified capture owners never qualify as unrelated kernel threads
Unattributable normal processes still fail closed
No signals issued to kernel threads by these changes
Original upstream REA source tree unchanged
No other project or service modified

validation.note: A short-lived capture can report settlement.state=unverifiable and residual coverage unknowns without cleanup failure; tests on longer-running processes reported settlement.state=quiesced.

hygiene.original_temp_roots: Historical retained /tmp/rea-process-* directories observed, not deleted without proving they contain no recoverable evidence.

maintenance_warning: These two fixes are reversible overlays in compiled dist modules. Rebuild/reinstall of the unchanged original REA may replace them. After any REA build, check both exact module hashes and, if necessary, reapply only through the pinned SHA-guarded recovery scripts and rerun the capture tests.
limitations: Scoped regression proof for these Linux process scenarios only; not an unrestricted certification of all 229 MCP tools.
